source.title: Choose K Elements With Maximum Sum

teaching.hint: Which answers become determined together when the threshold value is the same?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Sorting by the threshold key creates growing eligible sets, but equal-key entries must all be answered before any is admitted.
solution_outline.approach: Process equal `nums1` groups in increasing order. Retain the largest at most `k` positive `nums2` values from earlier groups and their sum; write that sum for the current group, then add its entries.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Before a group is answered, the retained values are the top `k` among precisely the indices with strictly smaller `nums1`.
solution_outline.correctness: Positive values make selecting the largest available `k` optimal. Delayed insertion excludes equals, and every original index receives its answer when its group is processed.
solution_outline.complexity: `O(n log n + n log k)` time and `O(n + k)` auxiliary space; use a wide sum.
solution_outline.pitfall: Inserting a value before answering its equal-key group violates the strict comparison.

common_wrong_turns: Allowing equal `nums1` values to contribute to one another
Keeping only the current maximum instead of the top `k`
source_fidelity_notes: Removed examples; explicitly retained positive `nums2`, strict comparison, original output order, and wide sums.
